text:
jess (customer): Hey team, after upgrading our app and reinstalling the SDK with `pip install -e .[http]` we started getting 401s from every API call. Works locally without editable install but fails in container image. stack trace shows ImportError for 'redwood.auth._headers' sometimes. Any ideas?

katie - support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste `pip freeze` and the exact install command + python version? Also are you using poetry or plain pip inside the container?

jess (customer): repro steps: Dockerfile uses python:3.10-slim, venv created, then `pip install -e .[http]`. `pip freeze` after install:```
redwood-sdk @ file:///src
httpx==0.24.0
certifi==2023.11.7
urllib3==2.0.4
```
pyproject has `httpx >=0.23` as optional. Locally (non-editable) we had httpx 0.23.3 and no issues.

katie - support: interesting — httpx 0.24 is fairly new and moved to urllib3 v2 in some images; could affect header handling. Two quick checks: 1) try `pip install 'httpx~=0.23'` inside container and retest; 2) run a tiny script to confirm auth header is sent:```python
import httpx
resp = httpx.get('https://httpbin.org/headers', headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer x'})
print(resp.json())
```

raj - eng: Looping in infra: editable installs create an egg-link to source which can pull local code that expects older httpx hooks. The ImportError about `redwood.auth._headers` hints at a packaging change where our module import path can be shadowed by a stray file in the app root. Two things: pin httpx to 0.23 to prove cause, and check for any `redwood.py` or `redwood` package in your repo that could shadow the SDK.

jess (customer): good catch — we do have a `redwood/` folder in our monorepo (internal utilities). Renaming it fixed the ImportError but 401s persisted until I downgraded httpx. After `pip install 'httpx~=0.23'` API calls started returning 200.

katie - support: thanks for the repro — sounds like a combination: package shadow + httpx version. For containers, editable installs + local package names are fragile. Workarounds:
- rename local package or use `pip install ./path/to/sdk` (non-editable)
- pin httpx to `~=0.23` for now
- ensure `REDWOOD_API_KEY` env var is set; the SDK reads env first so it's a reliable fallback

raj - eng: we opened an internal ticket. Quick technical note: httpx 0.24 changed default header merging when using `Client()` + event hooks; some of our internal auth helper code relied on older semantics. We'll release an SDK patch that normalizes header injection across httpx 0.23+ and handles editable-installed source layout more defensively. ETA: patch release 0.21.4 tomorrow.

deploy-bot: Release window scheduled: SDK 0.21.4 - will include httpx compatibility fix and extra import-safety checks.

katie - support: For your immediate deploy, two safe options: 1) pin httpx~=0.23 in your app, 2) install the SDK non-editable (`pip install /src/redwood-sdk`) or from wheel. If you want, I can draft a short Dockerfile snippet for the latter.

jess (customer): Dockerfile snippet helped, switched to wheel install and pinned httpx, all green now. Appreciate the quick triage! :tada:

raj - eng: we'll follow up in a separate support email with the patch notes and recommend a migration plan (once 0.21.4 publishes, it will accept httpx 0.23/0.24 without header regressions).

katie - support: marking this thread resolved — reopen if you hit anything after the SDK patch. Thanks for the detailed repro, it made triage fast. :raised_hands:
